newsitem.title: UK: KPMG sees volatile start for UK new issues in 1997.
newsitem.headline: KPMG sees volatile start for UK new issues in 1997.

text.p: Accountants and consultants KPMG said in a survey of the British new share issue market on Monday that the market in 1997 was set to be characterised by a busy and volatile start, before a hiatus around an expected election.
The head of new issues at the firm's corporate finance division, Neil Austin, said there was the possibility of "a large number of issues trying to beat the election".

If so, investors could afford to look closely at them and take their pick, he added. "The market will probably be quieter during during the election and for a while afterwards,...but I expect an upturn from the middle of the year," Austin said.
Nervousness in the stock market generally towards the year end took the edge off a strong year for new issues in 1996, KPMG concluded in its review of the last 12 months.
The company's preliminary data for 1996 showed that the total value of London flotations was 10.10 billion stg, just below the 10.14 billion stg record of 1994.

The average size of the year's 119 recorded new issues was the highest ever, it added, at 110 million stg -- in part due to the success of the Alternative Investment Market (AIM) in attracting smaller firms away from the main market.
